newsitem.title: USA: Nichols' Oklahoma bombing trial set for September.
newsitem.headline: Nichols' Oklahoma bombing trial set for September.

text.p: Terry Nichols, the co-defendant of Timothy McVeigh in the Oklahoma City bombing case, will go on trial on September 29, attorneys said on Thursday.
Nichols' lead attorney Michael Tigar told reporters the trial date was set during a closed-door meeting between U.S. District Judge Richard Matsch and prosecution and defense attorneys in Denver.

Nichols' trial will take place in the same Denver courtroom where McVeigh was convicted and sentenced to death by a federal jury earlier this month. Tigar said he has not yet decided whether to request a change of venue.

Prosecutors allege Nichols conspired with McVeigh to blow up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in downtown Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995. The blast killed 168 people and was the worst terrorist attack ever on U.S. soil.
Chief prosecutor Larry Mackey said the government's case will center on a statement Nichols gave to FBI agents two days after the bombing.
Tigar said in a recent television interview that Nichols helped McVeigh for several months but did not know that McVeigh was planning to bomb the federal building.
